Don't miss Saturn shine close to the moon tonight

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (395 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset tonight (Nov.
  • According to recent reports, saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S.
  • Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset tonight (Nov. 20), presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby.

According to recent reports, saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length.

Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.

The moon will present a spectacular target through the eyepiece of a 6-inch telescope, as the terminator line separating night from day creeps ever closer to its western edge. It's a great time to explore the 110 km-wide Gassendi Crater on the edge of Mare Humorum as its eastern rim and central peaks throw intense shadows across its interior.

Slewing your telescope over to Saturn will reveal details and subtle variations in the cloud surface of the gas giant, along with its iconic ring system, which is gradually becoming more visible following its ring plane crossing in March 2025.

Depending on viewing conditions, you may also notice a shoal of bright, star-like points of light surrounding Saturn's disk, which represent the large moons Titan, Dione, Tethys, Rhea and Iapetus.

Interested in seeing the planets of the solar system up close for yourself? Then be sure to check out our picks of the best telescopes available in 2026, including the Celestron NexStar 8SE, which we rate as the best motorized scope out there.

Editor's Note: If you would like to share your planetary astrophotography with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

Anthony Wood joined Space.com in April 2025 after contributing articles to outlets including IGN, New Atlas and Gizmodo. He has a passion for the night sky, science, Hideo Kojima, and human space exploration, and can’t wait for the day when astronauts once again set foot on the moon.

Boro beat Bristol City 2-0; Stoke 1-0 Birmingham.

Scott Parker still winless as West Ham held by Preston.

Middlesbrough scored a goal either side of half-time to climb to the top of the Championship with a 2-0 win that piled further pressure on the Bristol City manager Michael Skubala.

Adilson Malanda’s header five minutes before half-time was followed by David Strelec’s finish in the 54th minute to secure victory. The three points were effectively secured before Middlesbrough head coach Kim Hellberg introduced the division’s top scorer, Will Lankshear, for the final 14 minutes from the bench after injury. Defeat heightened the frustrations being felt by Bristol City, who have won just one of their last eight matches, as they dropped to 18th.

Recent findings suggest that hellberg later called Strelec “a brilliant human being” after the Slovakia striker’s first goal since May. “It was a massive moment for David. He has been very good since coming back, he’s shown how good he is in these two games. That goal was a beautiful team goal and he is a top player – you could see how happy he was.”.

According to recent reports, george Hirst scored the only goal as 10-man Stoke moved into the automatic promotion places with a 1-0 victory against Birmingham. Hirst broke the deadlock in the early stages of the second half before Luca Bombino was shown a second yellow card for the hosts in the 63rd minute. The two teams were level on points at the start of the day, with both having won their last three games, but it was Stoke who prevailed as Hirst scored for the first time since early September.

Adam Armstrong scored his fourth goal in five games and Rafiki Saïd his first for the club as Wolves beat Charlton 2-1 at Molineux. The dominant hosts put their first-half frustrations behind them to score twice in four minutes shortly after the break – both set up by Matheus Mané – before Matty Godden’s 81st-minute consolation rattled a few home nerves. Victory extended Wolves’ unbeaten run to seven games.

According to recent reports, ashley Williams began life as Swansea’s interim head coach with a draw against the club who highlighted him the door as a 16-year-old 25 years ago. West Brom led twice through goals from Isaac Price and Rabby Nzingoula, but Swansea levelled each time thanks to Moussa Yeo and Elijah Just. All the goals came in an eventful first half, with the crucial moment being a penalty save by the Swansea goalkeeper Lawrence Vigouroux to deny Price.

According to recent reports, stockport took over top spot in League One with a 3-0 victory away at Cambridge. Second-half efforts from Oliver Norwood and Ethan Ennis and an own goal from Gassan Ahadme sent County three points clear of Huddersfield, who lost by the same scoreline against Leicester, with Louis Page netting the only goal.

Oxford are level on points with the Terriers after dramatically beating nine-man Wycombe 4-3. Wanderers led 3-0 but Dan Casey and Luke Leahy both saw red in the second half, and Gatlin O’Donkor’s goal five minutes into injury time completed the comeback.

It has been revealed that A Nahki Wells double helped in-form Luton come from behind to beat Burton 2-1 while a very late goal from Sean Grehan helped Doncaster draw 2-2 against high-flying Bradford. Managerless Blackpool were beaten 2-1 by Wigan following Ian Evatt’s sacking and Peterborough beat Plymouth 2-0. There was a notable away victory for struggling Bromley against Reading, Victor Adeboyejo scoring the only goal, while Leyton Orient dispatched AFC Wimbledon 4-1. PA.

In a recent development, tonda Eckert urged Cyle Larin to keep channelling his inner Robert Lewandowski after his goal helped Southampton to a 2-0 victory against Derby. The Canada forward bundled in his eighth goal of the season on his return from a hamstring injury before Divin Mubama settled the contest in stoppage time.

Eckert who crossed paths with Poland great Lewandowski when coaching at Bayern Munich, remarked: “I think it was an unbelievable finish. Those are the finishes you can’t teach a striker. You have that in your blood. I think Lewandowski said once that if the manager tells you how to move in the box as a No 9 you should do your own thing. Larin knows what to do in the box, there is nothing to tell him.”.

In a recent development, alex Neil fumed at what he called “over-zealous” officiating in Millwall’s 1-0 loss against QPR. While Neil had no complaints about the red card shown to left-back Zak Sturge after just 15 minutes, he took problem with the punishments meted out to him and his backroom staff. The Scot was shown a yellow card following an altercation with the QPR forward Paul Smyth, with his assistant Martin Canning also being booked later on after the goalkeeping coach, Dean Thornton, had been sent from the dugout. Nicolas Madsen’s goal proved decisive at The Den as QPR won away from home for the first time since August and inflicted a third straight defeat on Millwall.

In a recent development, neil said: “I’ve been coaching for well over a decade at this level and I’ve been booked less than a handful of times. Any time we spoke to the fourth official, he was dishing out bookings like confetti.”.

Sheffield United returned to winning ways as they breezed past struggling Watford with a 4-0 victory at Bramall Lane. Two early Ben Brereton Díaz goals and second-half strikes from Jordan Ayew and Sydie Peck sealed a win that was all too easy for the hosts. It was a feisty affair, with referee Tim Robinson handing out 13 yellow cards – much to the disapproval of both sets of fans.

Norwich came from behind to beat Cardiff 2-1 and make it five successive league wins. Yousef Salech put Cardiff ahead three minutes into the second half but the hosts rapidly regrouped and were back on level terms on 62 minutes when the in-form Paris Maghoma curled in from just outside the area. The winner arrived six minutes later when Mathias Kvistgaarden’s penalty was saved by Nathan Trott but the Danish striker reacted quickly to stab home the rebound.

League Two leaders Salford held on to a 1-1 draw against Accrington despite being reduced to nine men. All the action came in the second half, with Elliot Bonds putting Salford ahead just after Daniel Udoh had been sent off. Donald Love equalised for Stanley before Bonds also saw red.

It has been revealed that aaron Lewis scored twice as Newport piled the pressure on Ian Holloway with a 2-0 win against Swindon at Rodney Parade. It was a 10th defeat in the last 15 games in all competitions for the visitors.

Barnet closed the gap to four points with two games in hand thanks to a 2-1 victory over Port Vale. Onel Hernández opened the scoring for Vale but was later sent off and Tom Knowles netted what proved to be the winner.

Dylan Duffy scored twice as third-placed Chesterfield defeated Shrewsbury 4-1 while Grimsby and York were both held to goalless draws. A more dramatic draw saw sixth-placed Crewe held 3-3 by Gillingham, with veteran Garath McCleary scoring an injury-time equaliser. Bottom side Crawley claimed their first home win in the league, beating Fleetwood 2-1, but fellow strugglers Rochdale lost a topsy-turvy encounter 3-2 to Northampton. PA.

It has been revealed that scott Parker’s stuttering start as West Ham manager continued in his first match at the London Stadium as bottom club Preston battled their way to a 1-1 draw. Parker is yet to taste victory in three games since he returned to the club. After Konstantinos Mavropanos headed home on the hour to cancel out Liam Lindsay’s early goal for the visitors, it seemed that West Ham’s attacking power would force a victory to keep pace in the promotion race. Instead, despite having 27 efforts on goal, they could not break Preston’s resistance and are now winless in their past five games.

Parker said: “I got here really early today and I had a vision of ending the day with three points and a brilliant performance. I got the brilliant performance, but not the three points, so in that sense, I am devastated. But with a rational head, there were a lot of good things, and if we played that game a hundred times, we would win every other time.”.

Sam Dalby’s fine effort cancelled out Josh Murphy’s powerful header as Bolton held Portsmouth to an entertaining 1-1 draw, while George Thomason struck a late winner as Wrexham secured a welcome 1-0 victory at Lincoln. It was a first away league victory for Phil Parkinson’s side since the start of September when they beat Millwall 2-0.

#82596. Latest Update: The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?

Latest Update: The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1163 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The electoral successes of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) have brought the party closer than ever to taking power in Germany.
  • This raises an even sharper question: what political ideas does the party stand for, which has been classified by Germany's domestic intelligence agency as a "suspected right-wing extremist" organization and, in several federal states, is already considered "confirmed right-wing extremist"?
  • Many political scientists have observed that the AfD has become increasingly radicalized since its founding in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The electoral successes of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) have brought the party closer than ever to taking power in Germany. For the 2029 federal election, it has set itself an ambitious goal: to see its co-chair Alice Weidel to become Germany's next chancellor.

This raises an even sharper question: what political ideas does the party stand for, which has been classified by Germany's domestic intelligence agency as a "suspected right-wing extremist" organization and, in several federal states, is already considered "confirmed right-wing extremist"?

Many political scientists have observed that the AfD has become increasingly radicalized since its founding in 2013.

"Viewed as a whole, the AfD is an extreme right-wing party that also displays tendencies associated with a fascist movement," noted Fabian Virchow, a researcher on right-wing extremism at Düsseldorf University of Applied Sciences, in an interview with DW.

Virchow identifies different factions and strategic tendencies within the party, some of which are at odds with one another. Party leader Alice Weidel, for example, is generally seen as a proponent of a free-market approach that seeks to keep the state as small as possible. Others, by contrast, favor a strong state shaped by an ethnically homogeneous people, among them Björn Höcke, the influential far-right AfD leader in the state of Thuringia.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Virchow sees a "normalization" of right-wing extremist positions within the AfD. In his view, this has made the party more attractive to neo-Nazi circles: "Today, many people see greater room for ethnonationalist and radical right-wing ideas.".

In a recent development, support for this observation comes from the latest findings of the Leipzig Authoritarianism Study, one of the most widely cited long-term studies tracking right-wing extremist attitudes in Germany. The researchers behind the study have identified a rise in right-wing extremist views within German society, including a growing acceptance of ideologies rooted in the tradition of National Socialism.

Particularly striking is the finding that around two-thirds of people with firmly entrenched far-right worldviews would vote for the AfD. According to the study, the AfD has achieved what earlier far-right parties in Germany never managed: "to unite large segments of the electorate with anti-democratic attitudes behind it.".

Recent findings suggest that the debate has been further fueled by several recent incidents within the party. In 2026 alone, numerous AfD politicians and staff members made headlines over alleged ties to neo-Nazi organizations:.

Sources indicate that in August 2026, police carried out a large-scale raid targeting fifteen people. Authorities suspect them of continuing the activities of the so-called "Artgemeinschaft." Before it was banned in 2023, the group was considered one of Germany's largest and most influential neo-Nazi cadre organizations. Particularly explosive was the fact that two of those targeted in the raid are sitting AfD members of the Saxony-Anhalt state parliament. Their attorneys deny the allegations.

Industry observers note that according to reporting by the German daily, Welt, four staff members of the AfD's parliamentary group in Saxony-Anhalt are former members of the now-banned "Heimattreue Deutsche Jugend" (HDJ), a neo-Nazi youth organization rooted in National Socialist racial ideology that organized paramilitary camps for young people. Two of the staff members held leadership positions within the HDJ and now work closely with AfD politician Ulrich Siegmund, who is seeking to become the AfD's first state premier in December.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, remarkably, both organizations, the "Artgemeinschaft" and the HDJ, are on the AfD's so-called incompatibility list, which is intended to draw a line between the party and extremist organizations and movements. In principle, anyone with a history of membership in such groups is supposed to be excluded from the party.

But the list appears to be little more than a dead letter. In 2020, former AfD federal executive board member Andreas Kalbitz was expelled from the party after failing to disclose his membership in the "Heimattreue Deutsche Jugend" on his application to join. Yet according to the news magazine Spiegel, he is once again working for the AfD, this time as a staffer for Saxony-Anhalt state legislator Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, who has since become deputy speaker of the state parliament.

The question of the AfD's relationship to National Socialism has dogged the party since its founding in 2013. Even in its early years, co-founder and first party leader Bernd Lucke sparked controversy when he described democracy and parliamentary politics in Germany as "degenerate," a term the Nazis used to disparage art and culture that did not conform to their ideological worldview.

In Germany, references to the Nazi dictatorship (1933-1945) under Adolf Hitler remain politically taboo because of the country's responsibility for World War Two and the Holocaust, the systematic mass murder of Europe's Jews.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

If AfD members or their staff have come under scrutiny because of past involvement in ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations, they have generally sought to distance themselves from those backgrounds or from the ideologies associated with them.

But how credible are these attempts at distancing? Laura Neumann* has worked with many people seeking to leave the far-right scene. She works for "Nordverbund Ausstieg Rechts," a network of organizations that supports far-right cadres and activists as they disengage from the movement. "A successful exit is the result of a professionally guided process," she noted in an interview with DW.

Neumann describes leaving the far-right scene as a challenging process of self-confrontation. "When it comes to someone leaving the movement, the first question I always ask is: How does that person talk about their past? Have they genuinely come to terms with it?".

Based on the experience of exit counselors, one principle generally holds true: the longer and more deeply a person has been immersed in far-right circles, the more difficult it becomes to distance themselves from those beliefs and affiliations.

DW requested a statement from the AfD's federal executive board regarding its handling of party members who were previously active in ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations. Individual lawmakers and parliamentary staff members were also asked to comment. None responded.

Recent findings suggest that the party's and its politicians' silence in the face of such allegations reflects an observation made by political scientist Fabian Virchow: "Within the AfD, there is no longer a perceived need to distance oneself from radical far-right positions. That is part of this process of normalization.".

Virchow claims that right-wing extremism appears to have advanced so far into the mainstream of German society that efforts to scandalize it now remain largely ineffective.

Sources indicate that * Editor's note: To protect the privacy of the staff member of Nordverbund Ausstieg Rechts, we have changed her name to Laura Neumann. Her real name is known to the editors.

Elliot Anderson halts Manchester City’s losing run but boos greet Fulham draw

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that manchester City are living in Premier League purgatory, without a win in four, but at least against Fulham they ended a three-game losing run.
  • Recent findings suggest that arguments will be made over Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal but City did not deserve anything more.
  • It is the first time Fulham have avoided defeat against City in 21 attempts going back to 2011, while City have conceded in nine consecutive games for the first time since 2019.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that manchester City are living in Premier League purgatory, without a win in four, but at least against Fulham they ended a three-game losing run. As they await their fate after being found guilty of financial breaches, their form has slumped. This passive draw was met with boos from the home fans.

Recent findings suggest that arguments will be made over Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal but City did not deserve anything more. The Norwegian uncharacteristically missed a number of fine chances as Rodrigo Muniz took advantage of City’s porous defence. They had to rely on Elliot Anderson to get anything out of the fixture.

It is the first time Fulham have avoided defeat against City in 21 attempts going back to 2011, while City have conceded in nine consecutive games for the first time since 2019. Enzo Maresca and his side’s problems go beyond legal wrangling.

City approached the game in the same subdued manner of the crowd, as is customary for a Saturday lunchtime kick-off. They offered little in the way of dynamism from the off. A couple of half chances were brushed off by Fulham, who were allowed to ease themselves into the game as slow-starters City conceded the opener for a fourth straight match.

It has been revealed that confusion between defence and midfield has repeatedly caused problems under Maresca, who saw Marc Guéhi cross the halfway line to press a throw-in deep inside the Fulham half. When the visitors won the first header, the centre-back was out of position and everything was far too simple from then on.

In the 16th ​minute, Oscar Bobb, a former City winger, shimmied and Muniz curled his shot into the top corner from the edge of the box.

Industry observers note that city finally found intent midway through the first half. Iliman Ndiaye’s dangerous cross found Haaland at the back post but he could not finish, allowing Bernd Leno to get his hands to the ball but whether the German had it under control is another matter. Haaland jabbed at the goalkeeper, nudging the ball through his grasp. Thomas Bramall and the video assistant referee gave the keeper the benefit of the doubt. Leno later told BBC Sport: “I had the feeling I controlled the ball and Haaland crashed into me and slid into me. It was a wet pitch. I was hoping VAR doesn’t overturn it. For me it was a foul.”.

• Fulham avoided defeat against Manchester City for the first time since September 2011 in all competitions, ending the longest ever winning streak one team has had against another in English football (20 matches).

• Manchester City have conceded in nine consecutive games in all competitions for the first time since a run to December 2019 (10), while they have conceded the opening goal in four consecutive Premier League games for the first time since a run to April 2012 (5).

Industry observers note that • Manchester City have trailed at half-time in four consecutive Premier League games for only the third time, after October 1995 and April 2006. Opta.

According to recent reports, maresca disagreed. “From my point of view, it’s quite clear that it’s not foul but I’m not the guy that decides, unfortunately,” he said.

City lacked a cutting edge. Phil Foden, given the nod over Rayan Cherki at No 10, could not get on the same wavelength as the misfiring Haaland, whose clinical finishing deserted him.

City continued to find it difficult as David Affengruber and Calvin Bassey put in fine performances at centre-back, snuffing out every danger. To find a way back, City needed to increase the tempo and Anderson obliged by volleying a cleared corner into the bottom corner from 18 yards.

Sources indicate that in an underperforming team lacking energy, the England international is a catalyst. He latched on to a Haaland flick-on but could not stay on his feet. The pair combined for a second time only for Anderson’s quick feet and cute finish to end with the ball slipping an inch wide in the 65th minute, City’s last meaningful opportunity.

Industry observers note that as the game ebbed to a close, City’s flaws were exposed as Fulham won the ball and Muniz was through on goal. Gianluigi Donnarumma was the last – and sturdiest – line of defence, repeating the feat against Bassey soon after as Fulham continued to look sharp and City blunt.

The jeers at the end stated it all.

#82589. Regular Tech Bros Are Worried About Honeypots

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1162 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Regular Tech Bros Are Worried About Honeypots

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1162 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When the founder of a cybersecurity firm hired Blaine Anderson as a matchmaker, it wasn’t just because the man was lonely.
  • The cybersecurity founder isn’t the only one.
  • “Even if you're not a CEO or at a major tech giant, these fears have trickled down to just regular professionals,” Simone Grossman, a Brooklyn-based matchmaker, tells WIRED.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When the founder of a cybersecurity firm hired Blaine Anderson as a matchmaker, it wasn’t just because the man was lonely. It was also, Anderson indicates, because he was “super worried about spies.”.

The cybersecurity founder isn’t the only one. As Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security dominates headlines and AI companies reportedly warn employees against “honeypots,” matchmakers say that more men with pretty normal lives are worried that their dates may have ulterior motives: accessing corporate secrets.

“Even if you're not a CEO or at a major tech giant, these fears have trickled down to just regular professionals,” Simone Grossman, a Brooklyn-based matchmaker, tells WIRED.

One tech worker, who requested anonymity in order to speak candidly, says he considers himself “highly selective” about the people he interacts with face-to-face.

Industry observers note that “Even though I could vet you from looking you up online, I can't help but still be a tad dubious,” he tells WIRED. On a scale from zero to 10, with 10 being the most anxious about espionage, he puts himself at a seven.

Even though the vast majority of tech employees likely won’t be targeted for romantic espionage, matchmakers say more clients have lately expressed concerns about women exploiting them for their corporate secrets. One Palantir employee told Andersen he wouldn’t date anyone who was a Chinese or Russian national. The anxiety has even become a marketing opportunity: One organization is pitching its upcoming line of AI executive girlfriends as a “zero espionage” alternative to human dating.

The concern isn’t entirely without basis. Some companies hire consultants to advise executives and lower-level employees with access to sensitive information on security risks, including the possibility of honeypots. Several of these consultants tell WIRED that raising the subject can be awkward.

“This one is always a very difficult message to deliver—to explain to, say, very sensitive engineers that maybe they're getting a lot of email attention because of their job,” says Isaac Stone Fish, founder and chief executive of the business intelligence firm Strategy Risks, “as opposed to the charm and force of their personality.”.

Industry observers note that amy Andersen, founder of Silicon Valley matchmaking organization Linx Dating (and no relation to Blaine Anderson), indicates that for clients concerned about their romantic partners’ intentions, she offers background checks, personal vetting, and NDAs. The security features are part of her “bespoke” packages that range anywhere from $75,000 to more than $500,000 for the “Founders Level.”.

Sources indicate that fear of romantic espionage is just the latest manifestation of growing distrust in the dating world. Shannon Lundgren, a matchmaker who has worked in San Francisco for 15 years, states that while she hasn’t necessarily heard more concerns about honeypots, she has noticed heightened skepticism around dating in general, as well as growing concerns about privacy.

The anxiety is particularly acute among AI workers, whose net worths—and therefore their perceived romantic desirability—are on the rise.

“If you're somebody who is a little bit shy or who is maybe a very stereotypical engineer type, to suddenly have your market value in the dating world change so drastically—you're already suspicious,” Grossman says.

To be worried about corporate espionage on top of all that, she notes, is “a mind fuck.”.

It has been revealed that honeypots and their state or corporate sponsors often look for “signs of vulnerability, such as an unhappy marriage, or someone seeking “excitement or adventure,” says Ira Winkler, a security consultant and the chief information security officer in residence at identity protection company Cloaked. Lonely people are opportune targets, regardless of marriage or relationship status.

The advice security experts give is somewhat obvious: If it seems too good to be true, it probably is.

“Really, if a beautiful woman approaches you, you know it's not for your personality,” Winkler tells his clients.

When tech workers do think of honeypots, they may gravitate toward the stereotype of a beautiful stranger who seduces someone at a bar and then extracts company secrets. “Any time one of us would take a trip to Asia, someone would always make a comment about getting a foreign girlfriend, or future wife, etc.,” one tech worker tells WIRED about his experience at a majority-male workplace. “We'd joke about them meeting a spy, but nobody really considered that seriously. Mostly they were just thinking of sex.”.

Sources indicate that that setup is largely a misconception. In reality, according to Greg Rinckey, founding partner of the legal services and consulting firm Tully Rinckey, most honeypot victims are groomed over time. “We’re talking sometimes months, could be years, where they're fostering that relationship,” he claims. Rinckey compares it to scammers trying to keep victims on the phone: The longer someone talks to another person and feels they know them, the more likely they are to trust them with sensitive information.

Catherine Marinis-Yaqub, a principal at the crisis and security consulting group Control Risks, tells WIRED that when people imagine the beautiful stranger at a bar, they may miss more likely scenarios, like an unexpected guest at a business meeting, a savvy networker at an industry conference, or a flirt at someone’s favorite coffee shop. Jensen Huang met Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese asset, for example, through a mutual business associate (who, according to The Wall Street Journal, also happened to be Alice’s husband).

For the man too scared of spies to make contact with a human romantic partner, there’s always artificial intelligence.

In a recent development, on Tuesday, in the wake of the Huang scandal, AI-relationship platform Joi AI launched a suite of "zero espionage" Executive Girlfriends. Brand director Julie Levin describes Joi AI as a “safe space” for exploration, where users can exchange NSFW texts, images, and videos with AI companions without judgment or rejection.

It made sense, she states, to extend that sense of security to honeypot-phobia.

“If they have some business secrets they don't want to share on a date or they feel nervous discussing with real people,” Levin states, “they can discuss them comfortably with their AIs.” (Levin assures WIRED that Joi AI employs several layers of security and that all of the data is anonymized.).

Industry observers note that high-profile executives are among those most at risk of honeypots, notes Winkler, the security consultant. They can also be some of the hardest to protect.

“It's really hard to influence somebody who's in control of the tech giant and just happens to be a sleazebag,” Winkler indicates.

It’s particularly difficult, notes Rinckey, when bosses think they’re the smartest person in the room and consider themselves immune to manipulation. It’s also not easy, he says, to be in the position of challenging an executive.

“Cocky, arrogant, and boisterous” chief executives make for desirable targets because “they love to talk about their business, and they love to talk about themselves,” Rinckey notes. In these situations, he says, “you don't even really have to pry them that much.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy.

Football players' union Fifpro indicates it is concerned by comments from Bayern Munich's hierarchy about Jamal Musiala's contract, adding the German club "should know better".

Musiala collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and the 23-year-old Germany international mentioned he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction".

Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness said earlier this month Musiala may never "regain the performance level he once had".

The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also questioned, external the lucrative contract extension the forward signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested, external the deal may need to be renegotiated.

"Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," remarked a Fifpro statement., external.

According to recent reports, "In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.".

Musiala may never return to his best - Hoeness.

Two collapses in four days - what's happening to Musiala?

Musiala, who joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy, came on for the German champions after 70 minutes in a 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday as he made his first outing since scoring in a 7-0 win against Union Berlin on 18 September.

He has made five appearances for the club this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist.

It has been revealed that "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala," added Fifpro. "Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

Industry observers note that "Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

"Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.".

Musiala's return to the Bayern side came in the same game in which England striker Harry Kane suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out "for the next few months".

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy.
  • That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban.
  • Industry observers note that harry Winks was the last academy graduate to score on his debut more than a decade ago – a feat that Kane also achieved two years earlier against Sunderland.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett indicated just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich.

That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett.

Industry observers note that harry Winks was the last academy graduate to score on his debut more than a decade ago – a feat that Kane also achieved two years earlier against Sunderland. Yet after Spurs decided to allow the England Under-21s striker Will Lankshear to join Middlesbrough in the summer, there was no chance that Williams-Barnett would be allowed to follow him out of the door. He became the 900th player ever to represent Spurs when he made his debut last year and the teenager left the field here to a standing ovation that he will never forget.

In a recent development, “I told him to play like he plays in the park with his friends, with the same freedom,” said De Zerbi. “And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembélé, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal. Luca is a special player. I’m not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He’s very young but at same time he’s very mature. He is older than his age.”.

Industry observers note that asked whether his protege has the potential to be compared to the Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi added: “Yes, I think so. One of the best things in my career I’ve seen today on the bus to the stadium. He was watching [clips] on YouTube of Ronaldinho, Hazard. I think he’s a special guy, because if one hour before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. Having the qualities is one thing but he has the passion for football, too.”.

After a promising start to the campaign, Ipswich’s momentum has stalled – they have now gone five games without a victory. But Gary O’Neil, who has already seen 16-year-old Max Dowman score twice for Arsenal against his side in the Carabao Cup, acknowledged that they had been second best throughout. “You need things to be perfect when we come to a place like this and we didn’t make things easy for ourselves,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that de Zerbi dropped a huge hint that Williams-Barnett could be handed his opportunity to start after two impressive cameos against Crystal Palace and Leeds. “Maybe, maybe,” he remarked on Friday. It turned out that the decision was actually taken last week, although the absence of Sandro Tonali due to illness forced Spurs into a reshuffle in midfield as Mateus Fernandes was handed the holding role.

Solanke has struggled to fill the void left by Kane since joining from Bournemouth in 2024 but looked in determined mood and he was inches wide with a swivel and shot from inside the area. A driving run from Williams-Barnett had the home supporters off their feet, with Solanke again going close from the resulting corner. It then needed a timely block from the teenager to stop Ipswich breaking downfield.

His big moment arrived less than 60 seconds later. Porro’s ball to the back post should have been dealt with by Abdoul Ouattara, only for a moment’s hesitation to allow Williams-Barnett to muscle in front of him and apply the finish with his knee. “He’s one of our own,” sang the Tottenham fans in delight.

Sources indicate that mohammed Kudus was unfortunate to see his superb effort from a free-kick cannon off the inside of the post and away to safety. Williams-Barnett will be disappointed not to have scored his second when he miskicked inside the six-yard box with the goal gaping. James Maddison was then denied by a brilliant save from Christian Walton and Williams-Barnett left the field at half-time looking very pleased with himself as he waved to his family in the crowd.

It has been revealed that his smile grew even broader after Darnell Furlong was left bamboozled by a direct run down the left flank before the youngster delivered the ball on a plate for Solanke to score his first goal here since March. The defeat could have been worse for Ipswich had it not been for Walton, and O’Neil will know they are in danger of being sucked into trouble if this winless run continues. There are no such concerns for Tottenham these days. Thanks to Williams-Barnett, their future looks much brighter than a few weeks ago.

What has changed in James Bond films over the decades

📅 05 Oct 2022 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1169 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios revealed on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.
  • This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.
  • The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios revealed on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.

This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.

The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".

Based on the spy novels by author Ian Fleming, the Bond franchise — about a British secret agent known for his charm and ⁠a ⁠fondness for martinis "shaken, not stirred" — is among the longest-running and highest-grossing in Hollywood history. ​​​​​​​.

The first film in the series, "Dr. No," premiered in London on October 5, 1962.

Playing the leading role, Agent 007, was an unknown actor: Sean Connery.

In the film, we are first introduced to his character as he sits in a casino across from an attractive woman who is about to gamble away her fortune. When she asks 007 his name, the camera pans to Bond lighting a cigarette. With a smoldering look in his eye, he utters the legendary words: "Bond, James Bond.".

In a recent development, shortly thereafter in the film, 007 receives an assignment to fly to Jamaica and investigate the murder of another M16 agent. He eventually tracks down a Chinese-German criminal scientist who is bent on destroying the US space program and achieving world domination.

In principle, this story is the basis of all of 25 James Bond films. Whether the villain is Dr. No, Blofeld, Goldfinger or Le Chiffre, they all aim for one thing: world domination. But to do so, they have to get past James Bond whose gunfire and wild chase scenes inevitably spoil their plans.

Although many fan forums consider "Dr. No" to be one of the best Bond films, the movie would never be made in the same way today.

Firstly, one could write entire books about the omnipresent sexism and machismo that the character James Bond has displayed over the decades.

It has been revealed that certainly there would have to be a thick chapter dedicated to the women in his films, who are typically portrayed as naive, willingly flinging themselves into Bond's arms, seeking protection. Sometimes they are sophisticated female antagonists who lose control at the thought of hopping into bed with the secret agent.

Recent findings suggest that whether friend of foe, each film had at least one Bond girl — and often more: More than 60 love interests have appeared in the films. Their names, like "Honey" or "Pussy Galore" would never be acceptable today. In more recent decades, female roles in Bond films have changed — as has Bond himself.

In the last five films in which Daniel Craig has played Bond, he is seen as a man who is tough on the outside and soft on the inside — and who is not always lucky with women.

Aside from the portrayal of women on screen, there are also plenty of other details in "Dr. No" that haven't quite stood the test of time.

Another sign of the zeitgeist in the 1962 film is that everyone smokes, which is a no-no by today's Hollywood standards. Cigarettes are found everywhere in the old film, from the casino to the hotel bar — and even the bedroom.

Smoking was commonplace in the US in the 1970s, so naturally this came across on the silver screen. In the 1970s TV series "Space: 1999" people were even depicted smoking on the moon, but by the 2000s, smoking was largely banned in many parts of the world due to its health risks.

One can also note in "Dr. No" that few people are wearing seat belts. When Bond drives off in his sports car to visit a woman, he is followed and a chase scene ensues. Bond, notably, is not wearing a seat belt.

It has been revealed that his pursuers eventually drive off a slope and die, of course — after all, they aren't wearing seat belts either and cars didn't have airbags at the time. The vehicle explodes, prompting 007 to say, "They were obviously in a hurry to get to their own funeral.".

In the older Bond films, all secretaries and receptionists are played by women, which in the 1960s, were considered standard female jobs.

Whether redheaded, blonde or brunette, secretaries are Bond's favorite targets for womanizing and they are all susceptible to his charms.

Throughout most Bond films, the agent has a romantic tension with Moneypenny, his boss's secretary, something which was not described in the original books.

It has been revealed that in the 2012 film "Skyfall" Moneypenny is given a first name: Eve, and we finally learn her backstory. In this film, she is no longer a hopeless secretary in love, but a top-trained agent who accidentally shoots Bond and is reassigned to desk duty as punishment.

In any case, today Moneypenny's job title today would probably be "Office Manager" or "Executive Assistant" rather than "Secretary.".

According to recent reports, in the film, Dr. No tells James Bond that he is the child of a British missionary and a Chinese woman from an upstanding family. However, the character is portrayed by Canadian actor Joseph Wiseman who is wearing makeup to make his eyes look more "Asian.".

While it used to be the norm in such movies to have East Asian characters played by white actors, today these cases of "yellowface" are frowned upon — just as it would be to wear blackface, putting black makeup on one's skin to portray a Black person.

If there was a "Dr. No" remake in the future, a Chinese actor would be more likely to play this role.

Daniel Craig already paved the way in modernizing James Bond by stripping away campy gadgets, punchlines and invincibility, replacing them with a grounded, psychological and emotionally vulnerable portrayal of a post-9/11 spy.

In a recent development, now it is up to Robert Pattinson to revisit the famous MI6 agent. Film critics believe his background will allow him to add dark sophistication and nonconformism to the iconic espionage role.

Throughout his career, Robert Pattinson has managed to combine roles in blockbuster hits and indie gems, from Bruce Wayne in "The Batman" to a disposable worker who is cloned every time he dies in "Mickey 17.".

Recent findings suggest that pattinson already has experience with classic spy archetypes: As the mysterious Neil in Christopher Nolan's sci-fi action thriller "Tenet," he assisted the protagonist in a time-bending espionage mission. He is also known for his eccentric personality and deadpan humor — qualities that could be useful for a modern Bond.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After the last international break of the year, Final Score pundit and former Swindon Town, Luton Town and Northampton Town striker selects his takeaways from the Championship, League One and League Two.

Stoke City are the Championship's form team, having taken 32 points from the last 39, but can they stay the distance in the promotion race?

Parkin: "I think everyone, probably me included, is really optimistic about their chances of this being the season they get it right.

"We're a fair chunk into the season now and I thought today's result was really notable because I believe this was their first win over anyone in the top eight. It felt like a bit of a statement win because Birmingham, apart from their defeat at Cardiff, have been really competitive in more or less every game.

"They've been able to just come out the right side of the scoreline and they've had to rely on their goalkeeper [Viktor] Johansson, who I think is one of the top goalkeepers at this level.

"I think there was an early shift in formation, going to a back three in the early part of the campaign, and I think that's proved quite key. They're keeping clean sheets and they've got a goalscorer in George Hirst.

Recent findings suggest that "I read a lot about Stoke City fans saying they're still probably short on forwards who are going to get them the goals. I know that [Jack] McGlynn has chipped in with a really impressive number from midfield, but for Hirst to get that substantial winning goal, that will have done his confidence the world of good.

"He's been promoted previously with Ipswich and there's no reason why he can't be Stoke's main man up front.".

Dejected Millwall boss Alex Neil.

Millwall have slumped to 16th after fighting for promotion in the last few seasons and they have lost five of their last seven league games.

Parkin: "They've had to deal with a horrendous injury crisis. It was at a level that I was struggling to think of a comparable club in the early part of the season. They were just having players go down week after week.

"There was one game in particular I covered against Wrexham and they had the walking wounded (out there), so I think they're still recovering from that.

"They've got some of the main players in [Casper] De Norre back fit now and available, but I think [Josh] Coburn was unavailable again today, and [Mihailo] Ivanovic is just making his way back - I would say they are three of their more vital players.

"Take away [Jake] Cooper at the back, who's been a mainstay for a number of years, and I think that trio I've just mentioned are so fundamental to their chances this season.

"They're still playing catch up to a degree, but Alex Neil has not pulled any punches in some of his interviews and he'll be disappointed.

"On the flip side of that, QPR are in a really good place at the moment, and are a much tougher proposition than maybe they would have been over the last couple of seasons.

It has been revealed that "I think Millwall will improve over time. I don't see them emulating what they did last season, but I think they can be optimistic they can get some better results once everyone's back available.".

Lincoln City management duo Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

Lincoln City are finding life in the Championship tough after romping to the League One title last season and they have lost seven of their last nine league games.

Industry observers note that parkin: "It's been a downward spiral and the home form's a bit of an issue. They just have the one win over Burnley there - and Burnley were in dire straits when they came.

"They've lost four in a row so that will be a little bit of a concern because they found a formula on the road in the early part of the season. But, yeah, you've got to do better in your home form.

Recent findings suggest that "I still trust they're going to be competitive and the majority of that squad, Jack Moylan apart, is still there from last season. You don't get over 100 points and then lose everything.

"That's always going to count for something when you've got the nucleus of that squad still together, even if it is in a higher division. So I think the spirit will remain amongst that group, despite the recent defeats.

It has been revealed that "They've got to start taking points off the better teams in the division as well. All their victories have come against teams who are in the lower part of the table, like Preston and Burnley.

"They won at Bolton and at Bristol City, so they're not really mixing it with the teams in the top half of the table at the moment.

"But I think the bottom line is the management duo would have absolutely taken being five points above 22nd at this stage of the season, so they've given themselves a good opportunity to stay in the division.".

Glum Barnsley boss Daniel Stendel.

Barnsley are four points from safety at the bottom of League One after Friday's defeat by Sheffield Wednesday in the South Yorkshire derby and are on course for a first return to the fourth tier since 1979.

In a recent development, parkin: "I think on last night's evidence, they're a better team than the league table suggests. That's an absolute certainty in my mind.

Sources indicate that "My one concern is where are the goals going to come from? For all their dangerous play, which is incredibly aggressive and energetic, with and without the ball, where are the goals?

"They throw caution to the wind and there's a real energy and youth about the side, which I actually really admired in defeat.

"It's just translating all that into goals and that was obviously one part of it against Wednesday, and giving away bad goals - they've conceded the most set pieces now in the division.

It has been revealed that "They conceded in that manner again, and because they play such a high line, they (also) get exposed by teams on the counter. Maybe that's a little bit of naivety. Maybe that's a little bit lack of experience, which they can go some way to mending in January when the transfer window opens.

It has been revealed that "But they may be adrift at the bottom if they don't turn things around soon. In short, I think they're a better team than a relegated team. But the most crucial thing in football, as we know, is putting the ball in the back of the net and that clearly is a problem for them at the moment.".

Crawley Town's Dylan Morgan celebrates scoring against Cheltenham Town.

Crawley Town boosted their chances of staying in the EFL when they recorded their first home league win of the season over Fleetwood Town and they have generated some momentum in their last few matches.

Parkin: "Former Leeds and Sheffield United manager Kevin Blackwell is in charge now till the end of the season. I was injured for the majority of his spell at Luton Town when he was my manager, but I'm kind of well versed in his methods and he will make them really hard to beat.

"That's always the first thing you want when you take over a struggling side, you need to stop shipping goals. You need to get them organised. You need to work on set-pieces and be a threat on that front. He will do all those things.

Recent findings suggest that "I think the three results in the league, two wins and a draw, have showed you that his methods have already come to fruition. His approach will be very different to probably what the players were being asked to do under Scott Lindsey.

It has been revealed that "It'll be a different kind of football. They'll play long at times, they'll want to play in the opposition's half. I think in terms of a proposal to get survival, he could very well be the man to supply that.

"They've chosen him after he was initially brought in as interim manager because the performances have improved across the last few weeks, despite the embarrassment of the FA Cup defeat to Wimborne.

"He's made them competitive very quickly and I think a lot of teams are going to be in for a real game when they face them.".

Sam Parkin was speaking to BBC Sport England's David Anderson.

Breaking: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (874 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, latest manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings.
  • Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism.
  • Sometimes football is simply a bit daft, a series of events linked by very little discernible pattern – and that’s how it was before the break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, latest manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.

Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard remarked. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.”.

Sometimes football is simply a bit daft, a series of events linked by very little discernible pattern – and that’s how it was before the break. Perhaps that’s just what happens when two of the three teams with the lowest possession stats in the league meet up; they can’t both not have the ball and so at least one side ends up having to do something they’re not used to. The second half was rather less frenetic and rather more coherent, as Palace’s full-backs played more conservatively.

“There are more positives than negatives from the game,” said Frank. “Offensively we looked like a threat. The effort and mentality I was extremely happy with. Defensively we conceded the first goal in a situation we 100% should have defended better, then an individual mistake. We’ll keep working on it, keep reinforcing the message in terms of what we want to do.”.

According to recent reports, in itself, playing without the ball is not a problem; absorbing pressure and striking on the break is a perfectly legitimate tactic and Lampard’s side have done it well at times this season. Palace are a slightly different case, given the obvious disconnect between their possession figure and Pierre Sage’s insistence he wanted to defend by holding the ball. That disparity, the sense that Palace’s players were unable to play as he wanted them to play, was probably the strongest argument in favour of cutting their losses quickly.

Frank abandoned the back three that had been the default not merely under Sage but also under Oliver Glasner, preferring a 4-3-2-1 with Anan Khalaili returning at right-back. It’s fair to say the Israel international is rather better going forward than at defending; playing at full-back rather than wing-back looked a real struggle for him – although he may feel there was mitigation in the way he was repeatedly left exposed. It took just five minutes for Coventry to open Palace up on that flank, three players converging on Yann Gboho as he backheeled a return pass to Jack Rudoni, who swept it across the box for Taiwo Awoniyi to stroke in.

• Coventry have won four of their last seven Premier League games (L3), with no side scoring more goals in the competition since the beginning of October (12, level with Bournemouth).

• Crystal Palace have conceded 27 goals in the Premier League this season; only in 1927-28 in the Third Division South have they conceded as many or more after 11 games in a league campaign (28).

• Only Brighton (6) have scored more goals from outside the box than Coventry City (4) in the Premier League this season, with 31% of the Sky Blues’ goals this term being scored from distance (4/13) – only Spurs (33% - 4/12) have a higher such share.

Sources indicate that • In what was his 115th Premier League game as a manager, Frank Lampard (pictured) has been booked for the first time, while he also didn’t receive a single yellow card in any of his last 31 Premier League games as a player. Opta.

It soon became clear, though, that this was never a game of only one goal. It was startlingly, thrillingly, almost disconcertingly open, with chances at either end. Yéremy Pino levelled, thrashing in after Jørgen Strand Larsen had laid off Daichi Kamada’s overhit cross with an outstretched heel. Then Khalaili missed his tackle, allowing Rudoni to surge forward and square for Tatsuhiro Sakamoto who, from just outside the box, lashed the bouncing ball into the top corner. Palace’s second equaliser was the result of a complete defensive breakdown. Pino’s initial cross was blocked and when he dinked in a second attempt, the only player even close to marking Strand Larsen was his teammate Kamada.

In a recent development, coventry’s threat had seemed diminished in the second half, partly as Palace looked less skittish and partly because Awoniyi aggravated an ankle injury and was unable to continue after the break. But those late substitutions gave them new impetus and, after a very silly first half, the game was won with a pretty silly goal.

#82575. The Smart Ring Goes to Church

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1361 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

The Smart Ring Goes to Church

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1361 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’re wearing a smart ring from Oura, Ultrahuman, or Samsung, the spike could prompt app suggestions like breathing exercises, meditations, or a physical reset like a short walk.
  • In a recent development, the first generation of Christian smart rings is here, joining other religious wearables like iQibla’s dedicated Muslim smartwatches, rings, and Hajj bands alongside “kosher” smartwatch apps.
  • Industry observers note that both are first, in their own ways.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that stressed? Heart rate elevated? If you’re wearing a smart ring from Oura, Ultrahuman, or Samsung, the spike could prompt app suggestions like breathing exercises, meditations, or a physical reset like a short walk. So far, so Silicon Valley. But now you can add reading the Bible to that list of self-soothing activities.

In a recent development, the first generation of Christian smart rings is here, joining other religious wearables like iQibla’s dedicated Muslim smartwatches, rings, and Hajj bands alongside “kosher” smartwatch apps. Two new devices in particular—Glorify’s Ring and Everblessed Technology’s Elah Ring—connect to hugely popular Christian prayer apps with tens of millions of users, and both claim to be the world’s first Christian smart ring.

Industry observers note that both are first, in their own ways. Everblessed’s $249 Elah Ring S1 went on sale in October and is shipping in the US. The $299 Glorify Ring launched in July, with reservations open and shipping set for January 2027, but 77,000 units of an earlier beta iteration, the Amen Ring made by faith tech organization ConfideIn (which merged with Glorify this May), were given away last Christmas. Everblessed manages the Blessed app, and Glorify has an eponymous app.

Sources indicate that another big player in prayer apps is Hallow, aimed at Catholics, backed by Vice President JD Vance’s Narya venture capital firm and celebrity ambassadors, with 24 million installs to date. Hallow’s toe-dip into wearables was a 2024 smart rosary with NFC embedded in the crucifix, made with Italian brand Ghirelli; Everblessed tried an earbud, necklace, and bedside device before settling on the ring design.

Head-to-head on design, the Elah and Glorify rings are both made from titanium alloy, with a thorn-inspired twist for Glorify and a minimalist band featuring a cross for the Elah S1, which is also IP68 waterproof to 5 meters.

Recent findings suggest that for now, the Elah Ring is slightly techier: prayer reminders come via the cross, which glows via an LED, and “gentle” vibrations; these can pulse at certain times of day or be triggered by changes in heart rate and stress levels, picked up by a photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor. Glorify’s CEO Henry Costa tells WIRED these emotion-based reminders will land on the Glorify Ring in six months; for now, you can set the times of day you want prayer reminders, track heart rate, blood oxygen, stress, and sleep via the optical sensor.

Recent findings suggest that one addition to the Glorify Ring that Costa indicates he personally uses “a lot” is recording prayers straight into the built-in mic. The ring has a light to signal when it's recording, and the app transcribes them. Everblessed CEO Ricky Xia says that, after consulting with pastors and users, the feeling was that voice notes on the ring were seen as “suspicious.” It’s available in-app, but most people don’t pray out loud, and too many features drain the battery life. (The Elah Ring runs for up to six days on one charge; Glorify for four to five days.).

According to recent reports, both companies see the smart ring nudges helping wearers prioritize meaningful quiet time, away from screens, while offering in-app Christian practices as an alternative to Eastern meditation. Glorify offers Bible study, courses, and meditations. Blessed has devotional “anchors,” Bible texts and audio, plus guided breathing. Xia says he’s happy if the Elah vibrates and a user picks up a paper Bible rather than the Blessed app, while Costa says he’s “crying out to use my phone less.”.

Sources indicate that both Glorify (founded in 2020, now merged with ConfideIn and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area) and Blessed (founded in 2023 and based in San Jose) operate in more than 150 countries. Perhaps the biggest difference between the two rings is their relationship to AI.

It has been revealed that xia is all-in, describing the S1 as an “AI-native” product, with a pastor-complementing, not-replacing FaithMate chatbot in the Blessed app, customized based on preferences, congregation, and depth of learning. ChatGPT is like a “good coworker,” he states, while FaithMate is designed to be “your friend” and an agent that can also handle secular tasks.

“A lot of our owners not only ask questions about the Bible but also ask about themselves, their relationships with their wives, they’re being bullied at school," Xia says, stressing safeguards around data storage, encryption, and privacy. "Everyone is going to have some AI that they trust, and how they view that is built on their personal stuff, their private vulnerabilities.”.

Costa is more circumspect, treading carefully on the consumer-facing side and noting that the Pope has weighed in with a 6,000-word encyclical on AI. A launch interview with CBN News garnered negative comments: “AI is Antichrist Information,” for one.

“The stance I’ve always taken is that our daily devotional is hand-authored by a team of theologians,” Costa states. “It’s prayed over, and that is a stamp of approval.” He criticizes AI slop prayer apps as inauthentic. Still, he says the Glorify team has already tested “many forms” of AI personalization: “Any time, if we do use AI, it must be very clear to the user.”.

In a recent development, smart ring owners were finding ways to add faith features to mainstream accessories before these rings came to fruition. For 20 years, timer and reminder apps have helped with prayer schedules, but recent examples are more creative. Heidi Campbell, professor of communication in religious studies at Texas A&M, refers to these DIY upgrades to the Oura ring and devices like the Muse headband as “spiritual mind-body hacking.”.

Oura owners on #christiantiktok chat about how they already use the ring’s stress and HR alerts as a prompt to pause and reflect, as per Elah.

Industry observers note that smart ring users flag changes in resting heart rate and sleep quality with scripture following their daily practice. “It’s really helpful for, like, what was inhibiting me from getting to a meditative or contemplative prayer state?” Campbell notes. “It takes some of the mystery out of prayer, I think, but that can also be positive. There is a way to do prayer well and not well.” Ring hackers can also dig into health stats during Lent, Ramadan, and Yom Kippur to analyze energy expenditure and how fasting periods affect their bodies.

AI-powered voice recordings and emerging attempts at emotion tracking are part of a new phase for smart rings, states Ekta Mittal, a senior analyst of connected devices at CCS Insight. These new “purpose-driven” features extend wearable tech into “new parts of consumers’ daily routines,” Mittal says. She suggests that while Glorify and Everblessed will add value for some, the rings are “not directly competing” with established smart ring giants like Oura, Ultrahuman, and Samsung.

The pandemic sped up the digital transition of many places of worship when congregations could not meet up in person, encouraging experimentation with social media. So it’s early days for Silicon Valley’s impact on organized religion. Researchers at the University of Würzburg in Germany, led by Ilona Nord, are studying the theological implications of using tech, including smart rings, for spiritual practices, investigating which values are baked into secular devices and apps.

Sources indicate that campbell suggests many Christian groups haven’t stopped to consider the unintentional consequences of cultivating spirituality via personal tech. “All of these things are about individualizing the practice, which is good, but the challenges are for religions which are really focused on communal aspects,” she claims. Not everyone has the money or connectivity to access these gadgets, but also, more existentially, “it puts spiritual development over communal development.”.

Xia points to the Blessed app’s communities, including its Healing Room broadcast feature, which lets pastors go live with sermons. It's not in the Elah app yet, but it's on the roadmap. Costa indicates communal practice is a core pillar, highlighting the “social layer” of public notes made on Christian texts in-app and an upcoming Glorify Ring feature which will allow a user to pair their device with a family member’s ring: “When your loved one is feeling down, you’ll get a buzz to check in with them.”.

#82571. NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth

NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (645 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that hate long-haul flights?
  • Imagine departing in 1977 and arriving in 2026, on November 18 at 11:16 a.m.
  • NASA's Voyager 1, a spacecraft launched almost half-a-century ago, has traveled a light-day from Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hate long-haul flights? Well, imagine having to travel 3,300 years to get to your destination.

Imagine departing in 1977 and arriving in 2026, on November 18 at 11:16 a.m. Central European Time to be precise, and then, not stopping but continuing the journey.

NASA's Voyager 1, a spacecraft launched almost half-a-century ago, has traveled a light-day from Earth.

Sources indicate that A light-day is the distance light covers in 24 hours — about 26 billion kilometers (or around 16 billion miles). Put another way: Light does in one day what it took the spacecraft 49 years, two months and 11 days to do.

But Voyager 1 is not only far away, it is also traveling at an incredible speed of 61,000 km/h (38,000 mph).

When Voyager 1 rolled out, it was in sync with a planetary alignment that was as rare as the spacecraft itself — one that happens only once every 176 years. It was the alignment Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, which scientists wanted to investigate.

Once the original mission was accomplished, Voyager 1 used the planets Jupiter and Saturn to perform a gravitational slingshot.

It flew close to each planet, got pulled and accelerated by their massive gravity, and swung around faster than before. And that is how Voyager 1 has achieved its speed.

In the vacuum of space, nothing slows you down.

On Valentine's Day 1990, from beyond Neptune, Voyager 1 took the only portrait of the solar system from the outside ever made by a spacecraft.

In 2012, it became the first human-made object to reach interstellar space.

Industry observers note that its journey is ongoing. In about 40,000 years — long after its plutonium power supply dies out — it will still be flying and pass by the star Gliese 445, which is more than 17 light-years away from Earth.

That's light-years, not light-days. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year. It will take Voyager 1 about 18,000 years to reach the one light-year milestone.

Voyager 1 is destined to wander the Milky Way "perhaps eternally," as NASA puts it.

The spacecraft is the first human-made object ever to be one light-day away from home.

"If you want to say 'hello' to Voyager, you send your message and then you go home and you wait two days before you finally get a response," says Suzanne Dodd, the mission's project manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

According to recent reports, but you do get a response. Even today it sends back data that helps scientists on Earth.

"[It's] still working great, sending back data from a region of space no other human-made craft has ever explored," says Kareem Badaruddin, the mission manager at JPL.

No story about Voyager 1 seems complete without mentioning The Golden Record, a phonographic record, that is part of the spacecraft's cargo.

The spacecraft is carrying other Earthly objects as messages and artefacts from Earth for extraterrestrials. But the Golden Record is what we tend to focus on because it contains soundbites representing languages and cultures from around our planet.

We're told it's very unlikely that any intelligent lifeform will ever receive the cargo or even know how to play The Golden Record.

Recent findings suggest that but if they do get the record and work out how to play it, the first thing they will hear is a controversial voice — not one of Earthly unity, as was the original idea. Those are the words of Kurt Waldheim, a former UN Secretary-General (1972-81) and Austrian President (1986-92), whose concealed wartime past as a German army officer in the Balkans surfaced a decade after Voyager 1's launch. It was alleged Waldheim had participated in Nazi crimes.

Elon Musk’s lawyer joining Tom Brady in buying Chelsea stake
